doc.title: Hubert Laws — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: The Met orchestra and joining CTI
title: Quincy Jones's Walking in Space session
summary: Laws recalls the all-star Walking in Space session at Van Gelder's, with Killer Joe, a tenor solo, and uncertainty about who drummed.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Let’s go back, because you had mentioned Quincy earlier, and of course Walking in Space, which again . . .

’69, June ’69. That for me is a seminal recording. You’re on it. It introduces my generation to Quincy in a new form. He’s doing music from Hair. So, for me, that’s another landmark recording. So you talk about that session, Killer Joe, Walking in Space, Bernard Purdie killing it, Rahsaan Roland Kirk killing on it. So if you could talk about that session.

That was at Rudy Van Gelder’s. I remember that. I do remember that most of the guys were there. It was not like we went and sweetened the session. Most of those guys were there. Ray Brown on bass. Goodness, I don’t remember who – was that Grady Tate playing drums on Killer?
Grady Tate on some, and then Bernard Purdie, definitely Bernard Purdie on . . .
He didn’t – Purdie didn’t play on Walking in Space. That was – when I say Walking in Space, wasn’t that a tune on the record?

Okay. Walking in Space and also Killer Joe, I think that was either Grady or somebody else played drums on that record – on that track. Then I know Freddie Hubbard did a solo, I did a solo, and they had the voices on Killer Joe. Walking in Space went through a lot of stuff, different rhythms. I think Purdie played on this thing – I played tenor saxophone, believe it or not, on one of those. Love and Peace?
I played a tenor saxophone solo on that. I think Pretty may have played on that track.
Oh Happy Day, I Never Told You.
Is that on the Walking in Space record?
That’s all on those. And then Dead End.
How come I don’t get a copy of that thing? I have it on lacquer, but I don’t have it on CD. I’d love to get that on CD. Walking in Space.
Has it been released on CD?
I’m sure it has. All Quincy’s stuff is out there now. And Valerie Simpson, oh.
You know what? I think Oh Happy Day, Purdie may have played on.
